1.s: In the wilderness of Sinai Moses counts all the men able to fight, tribe by tribe. The Levites are not counted; they care for the tabernacle.
1.d: The Hebrew title, be-midbar, means “In the wilderness”; the English name comes from the Greek Bible and its two censuses [[easton:Numbers-Book]] [[nabre:numbers/0]]. This count was mainly for war, so the Levites were counted separately [[nabre:numbers/1]]. The total is 603,550 men [[bible:Numbers 1:46]].

2.s: The camp is arranged with three tribes on each side of the tabernacle, Judah leading on the east.
2.d: The tribes camp by their banners around the Tent of Meeting, with Judah on the east toward the sunrise [[bible:Numbers 2:2-3]]. God’s dwelling is at the centre of the camp [[bible:Numbers 1:53]].

3.s: The Levites are counted and assigned duties, taking the place of Israel’s firstborn.
3.d: God takes the Levites in place of Israel’s firstborn, whom he made his own on the night he struck the firstborn of Egypt [[bible:Numbers 3:12-13]].

4.s: Duties of the Levite clans of Kohath, Gershon and Merari for carrying the tabernacle.
4.d: After the priests cover the holy things, the Kohathites carry them, but they must not touch them or even look at them, or they will die [[bible:Numbers 4:15]] [[bible:Numbers 4:20]].

5.s: Unclean people are sent outside the camp, wrongs are repaid with an extra fifth, and the ritual for a wife suspected of unfaithfulness.
5.d: Wronging another person is also a sin against the LORD: it must be confessed and repaid in full with a fifth added [[bible:Numbers 5:6-7]].

6.s: The Nazirite vow, and the priestly blessing: “Yahweh bless you and keep you; Yahweh make his face to shine on you…”.
6.d: Nazir means “set apart”; Samson, Samuel and John the Baptist were Nazirites for life [[nabre:numbers/6]]. The word “peace”, shalom, includes happiness, health, friendship and all well-being [[nabre:numbers/6]]. Words almost identical to the blessing were found on two small silver scrolls from about 650 BC, the earliest known fragment of a biblical text [[ref:vandam-amulets]].

7.s: The twelve tribal leaders bring identical offerings over twelve days for the altar’s dedication.
7.d: Each of the twelve leaders brings the same gifts, recorded one by one [[bible:Numbers 7:12-83]]. Then Moses hears God’s voice from above the mercy seat, between the cherubim [[bible:Numbers 7:89]].

8.s: The lamps are set up, and the Levites are purified and presented to God.
8.d: Only priests were “consecrated”; the Levites were “cleansed”, made ritually clean for their work [[nabre:numbers/8]]. They serve from twenty-five to fifty [[bible:Numbers 8:24-25]].

9.s: The second Passover is kept, with provision for those who were unclean. The cloud over the tabernacle signals when to move and when to stay.
9.d: Israel travels when the cloud lifts and camps when it settles, “at the commandment of Yahweh” [[bible:Numbers 9:17-18]].

10.s: Silver trumpets signal assemblies and departures; Israel sets out from Sinai. Moses prays, “Rise up, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered.”
10.d: The march through the wilderness resumes after the long stay at Sinai [[nabre:numbers/10]]. Moses’s words when the ark sets out, “Rise up, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered”, are echoed in Psalm 68:1 [[bible:Numbers 10:35]] [[bible:Psalm 68:1]].

11.s: The people complain about the manna and crave meat. Seventy elders receive God’s Spirit, and quail arrive, followed by a plague.
11.d: Moses wishes that all the LORD’s people were prophets [[bible:Numbers 11:29]]; at Pentecost Peter proclaims the Spirit poured out on all [[bible:Acts 2:17]]. Paul warns Christians not to grumble as Israel did [[bible:1 Corinthians 10:10]].

12.s: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses, and Miriam is struck with a skin disease until Moses prays for her.
12.d: The real reason for the complaint seems to be jealousy of Moses’s authority, and the Cushite wife is probably Zipporah [[nabre:numbers/12]]. God speaks with Moses directly, “mouth to mouth” [[nabre:numbers/12]] [[bible:Numbers 12:8]].

13.s: Twelve spies explore Canaan and return with huge grapes. Ten say the people are too strong; Caleb says, “Let’s go up at once”
13.d: Hoshea and Joshua are forms of one name meaning “the LORD saves”, the same name as Jesus [[nabre:numbers/13]]. The Nephilim, “fallen ones” (“giants” in the Greek Bible), recall Genesis 6:4 [[nabre:numbers/13]].

14.s: The people refuse to enter the land and want to return to Egypt. God sentences that generation to forty years in the wilderness; only Caleb and Joshua will enter.
14.d: Moses appeals again to God’s character as revealed at Sinai [[bible:Numbers 14:18]] [[bible:Exodus 34:6-7]]. The grumblers are given what they asked for [[nabre:numbers/14]]; their lack of trust is a warning to Christians in 1 Corinthians 10:10 and Hebrews 3 [[nabre:numbers/14]] [[bible:Hebrews 3:17-19]].

15.s: Laws for offerings in the land to come, and tassels on garments to remind Israel of God’s commands.
15.d: The tassels remind Israel of God’s commands [[bible:Numbers 15:38-39]]. In Jesus’s time all devout Jews wore them, Jesus included [[nabre:numbers/15]] [[bible:Matthew 9:20]].

16.s: Korah, Dathan and Abiram rebel against Moses and Aaron; the ground swallows them, and fire consumes their followers.
16.d: Aaron stands “between the dead and the living”, and the plague stops [[bible:Numbers 16:48]]. Jude names “Korah’s rebellion” as a warning [[bible:Jude 1:11]].

17.s: Aaron’s staff buds, blossoms and produces almonds, confirming God’s choice of him as priest.
17.d: A staff was a sign of authority, and the Hebrew word for staff also means “tribe” [[nabre:numbers/17]]. Aaron’s rod that budded is later said to be kept in the ark [[bible:Hebrews 9:4]].

18.s: Duties and support of priests and Levites: God is their inheritance, and they receive the tithes.
18.d: Priests and Levites owned no land of their own; certain cities were given them to live in [[nabre:numbers/18]]. “A covenant of salt” probably recalls eating salt together to make an agreement unbreakable [[nabre:numbers/18]]. Paul draws on these rules for supporting ministers [[bible:1 Corinthians 9:13]].

19.s: The red heifer: its ashes in water cleanse those who have touched a dead body.
19.d: Early Christian writers saw the heifer killed outside the camp as a figure of Jesus’s death outside Jerusalem, and its water as a figure of baptism [[nabre:numbers/19]]. Hebrews contrasts outward cleansing with Christ cleansing the conscience [[bible:Hebrews 9:13-14]].

20.s: Miriam dies. At Meribah Moses strikes the rock in anger instead of speaking to it, and God says he will not enter the land. Aaron dies on Mount Hor.
20.d: Kadesh means “holy” and Meribah “contention” [[nabre:numbers/20]]. The text does not make clear what lay behind Moses’s and Aaron’s failure; striking twice may show a lack of faith [[nabre:numbers/20]] [[bible:Numbers 20:12]]. The Edomites were descended from Esau, Jacob’s brother [[nabre:numbers/20]].

21.s: Venomous snakes bite the people; whoever looks at the bronze serpent Moses lifts up lives. Israel defeats Sihon and Og.
21.d: John’s Gospel sees the bronze serpent as a figure of the crucifixion [[nabre:numbers/21]] [[bible:John 3:14]]. King Hezekiah later broke it up, because people were burning incense to it [[nabre:numbers/21]] [[bible:2 Kings 18:4]].

22.s: Balak, king of Moab, hires the seer Balaam to curse Israel. On the way Balaam’s donkey sees an angel and speaks.
22.d: Balaam was known in tradition as a diviner [[nabre:numbers/22]]. The Deir ‘Alla inscriptions, found in Jordan, support placing his homeland east of the Jordan [[nabre:numbers/22]]. The angel is called an “adversary”, in Hebrew satan [[nabre:numbers/22]].

23.s: Balaam tries to curse Israel but can only bless: “God is not a man, that he should lie.”
23.d: “God is not a man, that he should lie” [[bible:Numbers 23:19]]. Balak keeps moving Balaam to new places, hoping for a different omen [[nabre:numbers/23]]; the blessing recalls God’s promise to Abraham [[bible:Genesis 12:3]].

24.s: Balaam’s third and fourth oracles: “A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel”
24.d: Early Christian writers and rabbis read the star and sceptre as a prophecy of the Messiah; Rabbi Akiba called a rebel leader “Bar Kokhba”, “son of the star” [[nabre:numbers/24]]. The New Testament never quotes it, and a link with the star of the Magi is doubtful [[nabre:numbers/24]].

25.s: Israelite men join in Moabite worship of Baal of Peor, and a plague follows until Phinehas acts.
25.d: Numbers 31:16 says Balaam was behind this sin [[bible:Numbers 31:16]], as Revelation also says [[bible:Revelation 2:14]] [[nabre:numbers/25]]. The zeal of Phinehas became proverbial [[nabre:numbers/25]].

26.s: A second census of the new generation, ready to enter the land.
26.d: No one counted at Sinai is left except Caleb and Joshua [[bible:Numbers 26:64-65]]. The new total, 601,730, is close to the first [[bible:Numbers 26:51]] [[bible:Numbers 1:46]]. Land is divided by size and by lot, and lots were seen as God’s will [[nabre:numbers/26]].

27.s: The daughters of Zelophehad ask to inherit their father’s land, and God agrees. Joshua is appointed to succeed Moses.
27.d: The law, like the one in chapter 36, keeps each family’s land within its tribe [[nabre:numbers/27]]. Moses asks that the people not be “as sheep which have no shepherd” [[bible:Numbers 27:17]], words used of Jesus’s compassion [[bible:Mark 6:34]].

28.s: The daily, Sabbath, monthly and festival offerings.
28.d: The daily offering is called the tamid, the “regular” offering [[nabre:numbers/28]]. The “day of first fruits”, the feast of Weeks, was known in Jesus’s time as Pentecost [[nabre:numbers/28]].

29.s: Offerings for the feasts of the seventh month: Trumpets, the Day of Atonement and Tabernacles.
29.d: The first day of the seventh month is now the Jewish New Year [[nabre:numbers/29]]. Booths, the most popular feast, had the most elaborate ritual: seventy bulls, falling to seven on the seventh day [[nabre:numbers/29]].

30.s: Rules about vows, and when a father or husband may cancel a woman’s vow.
30.d: A vow is a promise to give something to God on a condition, while a pledge binds oneself to do or avoid something [[nabre:numbers/30]]. Jesus teaches, “let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’” [[bible:Matthew 5:33-37]].

31.s: Israel wars against Midian, and the spoils are divided. Balaam is killed.
31.d: This resumes the campaign against Midian from chapter 25 [[nabre:numbers/31]], aimed at the Midianites living near Israel’s camp [[nabre:numbers/31]]. Balaam is killed among them [[bible:Numbers 31:8]].

32.s: The tribes of Reuben and Gad, and half of Manasseh, ask to settle east of the Jordan, promising to fight alongside the others.
32.d: These lands were once the kingdom of Sihon, between the Jabbok and the Arnon [[nabre:numbers/32]]. Moses warns, “be sure your sin will find you out” [[bible:Numbers 32:23]].

33.s: A list of Israel’s camping places from Egypt to the plains of Moab.
33.d: Moses records the list of stages [[bible:Numbers 33:2]]. It is not complete: its forty camping sites probably match the forty years on purpose [[nabre:numbers/33]].

34.s: The boundaries of the promised land, and leaders to divide it.
34.d: The Great Sea is the Mediterranean, and the Sea of Chinnereth is the Sea of Galilee [[nabre:numbers/34]]. Lebo-hamath, in the north, marks the edge of Israel’s ideal territory [[nabre:numbers/13]] [[bible:Numbers 34:8]].

35.s: Forty-eight towns for the Levites, and six cities of refuge for those who kill someone by accident.
35.d: The “avenger of blood” is the go’el, the next of kin, often translated “redeemer” [[nabre:numbers/35]]. The law develops Exodus 21:12–14 [[nabre:numbers/35]]. Hebrews speaks of those who have “fled for refuge” to the hope set before us [[bible:Hebrews 6:18]].

36.s: Daughters who inherit land must marry within their tribe, so the land stays with each tribe.
36.d: Without this rule, at the jubilee the land would pass for good to another tribe [[nabre:numbers/36]]. The book ends with the people waiting for God’s promise of the land [[nabre:numbers/0]].
